descriptionChirho: To physically shut or close a door, gate, or opening; Arabic أَغْلَقَ (aghlaqa 'to close') and سَدَّ (sadda 'to block up'); Korean 닫다 (datda 'to shut/close'); Swahili -funga ('to close/lock'); includes active Qal forms (perfect, imperfect, imperative, infinitive, active participle) and Qal passive participle in the sense of 'shut/closed' (state of being physically closed)

Of gold: refined, pure, shut up (i.e., smelted and purified); Arabic خَالِصٌ (khalisun 'pure, genuine') distinct from أَغْلَقَ; Korean 순수한 (sunsuhan 'pure'); Swahili safi ('clean, pure'); a specialized metaphorical extension of 'shut' applied exclusively to precious metals

Passive/reflexive: to be shut, to be closed, to be confined; Arabic تُغْلَقُ (tughlaqu 'it is closed'), أُغْلِقَتْ (ughliqat 'was closed'), حُبِسَتْ (hubisat 'was confined'), تُحْبَسُ (tuhbasu 'she is imprisoned'); Korean 닫히다 (datchida 'to be closed'), 격리되다 (gyeokri-doeda 'to be quarantined'); Swahili -fungwa (passive of -funga); includes being shut out or quarantined (e.g., Miriam in Num 12)

Hifil causative: to cause to be shut up, to quarantine or isolate a person (especially in Levitical skin-disease inspection, Lev 13-14); Arabic يَحْجُزُ (yahjuzu 'to quarantine/isolate') from root حجز distinct from أسلم 'deliver'; Korean 격리하다 (gyeokri-hada 'to quarantine'); Swahili -tenga ('to separate/isolate'); semantically distinct from Hifil 'deliver up' by the confinement rather than transfer to another party

To deliver up, surrender, or hand over a person to an enemy or authority; Arabic أَسْلَمَ (aslama 'to hand over/surrender'), يُسَلِّمُ (yusallimu 'to deliver'), تَسْلِيمُ (taslimu 'delivering') — all from root س-ل-م, completely distinct from أَغْلَقَ 'shut'; Korean 넘겨주다 (neomgyeojuda 'to hand over'), 내주다 (naejuda 'to give over'); Swahili -kabidhi ('to hand over'), -toa ('to give out'); attested in both Hifil and some Piel forms

Piel intensive: to shut up, confine, or imprison a person; Arabic حَبَسَ (habasa 'to imprison/confine') and يُسْجَنُونَ (yusjanuna 'they are imprisoned') — distinct roots from both أَغْلَقَ 'shut' and أَسْلَمَ 'deliver'; Korean 가두다 (gaduda 'to confine/imprison'); Swahili -funga ('to lock up'), -fungwa ('to be locked up'); intensive confinement stronger than simple Qal 'shut'

labelChirho: be firmly shut, be barred (Pual passive)
descriptionChirho: Pual passive intensive: to be firmly shut, locked, or barred; Arabic أُغْلِقَ (ughliq 'was closed'), مُقفَلَةٌ (muqfala 'barred/bolted') — note مُقفَلَة from root ق-ف-ل 'to lock/bolt' indicating a stronger closure than simple أُغْلِقَ; Korean 닫혔다 (datchyeotda 'was shut'); Swahili -fungwa ('was closed/locked'); passive of the intensive Piel, denoting a firmly secured or barred state
